assumptions: one unconditional key per canonical initial/final
Y and YU use the same initial key; zero branches
argument: Y overlaps every ordinary onset and needs its own bucket.
Only f with j/q/x is a disjoint ordinary pair whose union fits 25 final keys. Exactly one such pair must merge.
A,E,W can attach only to j/q/x, and cannot attach to the one already hosting f. W conflicts with both A and E, so W occupies one remaining bucket and A/E the other.
Each of f,W,A/E is therefore merged with a member of j/q/x. Their identical 14-final sets form T.
U has 12 finals all co-occurring under m; every U final occurs under f,W,A or E. Thus U and T form a forced 26-clique.
